summary: This is DIAGNOSIS action 2 almost word for word. It is the first small-M NVFP4 design with no N16 padding, no wgmma smem staging, no split-K or tickets and no grid spins, and its ~2.6-3.3 TB/s target is physically reachable at T=1. Run it as the stage-1 okc check. Fix two things first: the gate threshold (new lesson: two interleaved rounds >= 1.03 with an IQR bound) and the missing zero-local-route canary.
justification: A. Mechanism. decode_1 is 46.4 us against an 11.4 us floor, and the Marlin pair is 35.4 us (85.8%) of it. The ~56 MB checks out against TASK: 8 local experts x 3 x I(1024) x 4096 x 0.5625 B is about 56.6 MB, which matches the 11.4 us floor at 4.8 TB/s, so the judge routing puts all 8 routes local at T=1. Repacking into 4608 B gate/up pair rows (2 x 2048 B codes + 2 x 256 B e4m3 scales) is lossless and lets one 1-D cp.async.bulk per span stream contiguous bytes, with no tensor maps. That also avoids the g_maps per-state failure class. ALU budget: at 3 TB/s on 132 SMs, each SM needs ~13 B/cycle, about 23 FP4 elements/cycle. At T=1, dequant plus one FMA per element is well under 1/4 of issue, so variant F is feasible. At T=4 the fp32-accumulate FMAs reach ~90+/cycle/SM out of 128 lanes plus dequant, so F may be ALU-bound there. The design already says variant M or a T=1-only restriction is the fallback. Reduce-free row ownership removes the cross-CTA reduction that caused the bs=1 slow mode (LESSONS: the w2 atomic cut it from 44/100 to 10/100). It uses no spins, unlike the dead cuda-fused-moe-bs1-persistent-* line. Prior: cuda-fused-split-i-moe-tiny-t (queued) keeps the wgmma rega consumer, and DIAGNOSIS holds that consumer at T<=7 (tiny-m-bucket16 46.0 vs 45.5 us). cuda-nvfp4-swapab-mma-persistent-small-m-inproc used padded swap-AB mma tiles and persistent scheduling and was 1.7-2x slower. The difference from both is real: this changes the consumer (register-resident x, no N16 pad) and the load path (contiguous row spans). It is not on any do-not-try list, and DIAGNOSIS explicitly says a stage on a new consumer is not a re-run. Expected directions match: only bs=1 moves, and bs=4 is a test, not scored. The M3 numbers (17-22 us, decode_1 ~28-33 us, +5.5-8% headline) follow from one of six equally weighted loads going 46 -> ~30 us. WEAKEST LINK: the 3.5 TB/s anchor is a bf16 result (0.5 elements per byte). LESSONS 172 says the 1-CTA/SM row-owner pure stream reached only 2.54 TB/s cold, and only the 2-CTA/SM qkv instance reached ~3.5. NVFP4 does ~3.6x more consumer work per byte (~1.78 elements/byte with scales), and every NVFP4 kernel so far has capped at 1.5-2.1 TB/s because of dequant and consumer issue. Transfer is therefore unproven. Also, ~56 MB at ~3 TB/s is an ~19 us kernel pair, short enough that ramp-up, the w13->w2 drain and tail effects can eat a large share. M2 (beating 35.4 us) is likely; M3 (>= 2.6 TB/s) is the real bet. Minor: the cited LESSONS line numbers are stale (C++20 is line 164, not 159; row-owner is 172, not 167).
confounders: combo-toprow-w13t1-d32-alignpar-postnorm-wg-align2 (master) runs w13 use_atomic_add at T=1 (W13_ATOMIC_MAX_TOKENS=1, 0.949 when live, routing-dependent). The prepare gate compares against master's T=1 path, so whether F1 went live in that process sets the bar. The 35.4 us incumbent comes from the board branch, where F1 gated off on skewed routing. Read the replaced kernels against master's own T=1 Marlin rows in the same profile, not against 35.4.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (landed, T<=32) removed most of the bs=1 slow mode. The replacement drops it at T<=4, so any bimodality in runs_ns now belongs to the new kernels. That makes runs_ns instrumentation essential, as the design says.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m / _post_norm_combine_kernel: kept unchanged, but it reads y[t, s] only where local_ids[t, s] >= 0. Kernel A must emit local_ids in master's [T, 8] layout ([-1] for remote) and write y rows at route index t*8+s. A route-order mismatch is a silent correctness bug, not a perf confounder.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (_align_small, 1.5 us at decode_1): it is unclear whether kernel A replaces it or runs beside it. If both run, ~1.5 us of front-end stays and the decode_1 row understates the GEMM win. Attribute by kernel time, not by row.
interference: No companion. This is a rewrite stage, judged on the replaced kernels' own time in the profile. Both milestones that matter (M1 correct; M2 replaced kernels <= incumbent) can be read from one run, because the prepare gate prints kernel-only TB/s and timings for both variants against master's path, and the profile shows the new kernel names when live. The landed items above change only the incumbent's bar (F1 at T=1), and that bar is measured in the same process. A revert companion would not disambiguate anything the gate print does not already show. The real risk to readability is the tiny-m-bucket16 failure mode: the gate keeps master and the check measures master. So the prepare log must print every variant's T=1 and T=4 cold-L2 kernel-only us and TB/s even when PATH CHOSEN = MASTER, so the next stage can be minted from those numbers.
rules_flags: Gate threshold: '>= 1.02x on the worse routing' with one measurement conflicts with today's LESSONS lines 25-27 (single-round 1.02x selectors mis-routed). Use two interleaved rounds, both >= 1.03, with candidate IQR <= 1.5x master's, or the scored row can come from a mis-routed cell. This is not a rule violation, but it is a correctness-of-attribution and regression risk.

Graph safety: the work map (expert list, CTA->span assignment, route rows) must be computed on the device from topk_ids each call, with a fixed grid sized for the worst case (T=4: up to 32 local routes and up to 32 distinct experts), and no host read of the count. The design says this; verify that the grid size depends only on T and on prepare-time constants.

State copies: the judge prepares several state copies (copies: 2). Per-call scratch (work map, h buffer, mbarrier error word) must live in each state, not in module globals (LESSONS g_maps). The self-check should replay a captured graph while alternating two states with refilled inputs.

Precision: bf16x2 products round each w*x to bf16 before fp32 accumulation. That is allowed (activations stay bf16, weights stay NVFP4, dequant happens in-kernel) and well inside 1.5% rel-L2. h must be rounded to bf16 exactly as SGLang's act_and_mul does, which the design states.
The prepare repack must be lossless from the original NVFP4 codes and scales, keeping the per-expert global scale. Store no derived or precomputed bf16 weights.
open_questions: Does kernel A replace master's _align_small at T<=4 or run beside it? It must produce local_ids in master's [T, 8] layout for _post_norm_combine_kernel.

Zero local routes: does the canary force a T=1 or T=4 routing with no local expert? The output must be zeros. _post_norm_combine_kernel stores zeros, but the w13/w2 kernels must not fault or hang on an empty work map, and the mbarrier rings must not deadlock when a CTA has no span. The canary lists counts 1, 2 and 8 only.

w2 dependency: will the w2 kernel's producer issue its weight bulk copies before griddepcontrol.wait? w2 weights do not depend on h. Prefetching them under the w13 tail is the cheapest stage-1 lever. Check that smem lets w2 CTAs co-reside with w13 CTAs at 2 CTAs/SM, or the PDL overlap is nil.

Span balance: with 264 CTAs (2 per SM) and 8 active experts at T=1, 33 CTAs per expert x 31 pair rows covers 1023 of 1024 rows. How are remainder rows and non-divisible active-expert counts (3, 5, 7) assigned without a tail CTA doing twice the work?
If variant F is ALU-bound at T=4 and M is chosen, padding 4 tokens to 8 doubles the B-operand work. Does the gate print both variants at both T so stage 2 can split T=1 (F) from T=2..4 (M)?
